subject.title: Windows: multiple gateway-down failure modes (kill-and-rebind restart loop, config-edit no-relaunch, browser launch crash, blocking pricing fetches)

question: Should this issue remain the canonical P0 Windows gateway-down umbrella while maintainers split the individual lifecycle, config repair, browser, pricing, CLI shim, and installer fixes into owned follow-up work?
rationale: The report spans stable gateway runtime, setup recovery, plugin browser behavior, provider CLI execution, and pricing defaults, so the correct split and product recovery UX require maintainer prioritization before repair automation should create a broad PR.

options.title: Keep Umbrella And Split
options.body: Keep this issue open as the canonical blocker and create or assign scoped fixes with live Windows proof for each failure mode.

options.title: Pick One Core Fix First
options.body: Treat the idempotent gateway ensure and single-instance cleanup as the first owned fix while leaving the remaining modes in explicit follow-up issues.

options.title: Require Fresh Reporter Repro
options.body: Pause implementation until the reporter or QA can reproduce each mode on current main, accepting slower progress but reducing mis-scoped fixes.

recommendation.title: Keep Umbrella And Split
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open as the canonical blocker and create or assign scoped fixes with live Windows proof for each failure mode.

likelyOwner.reason: This account is the strongest current routing signal for Windows gateway service and lifecycle work among the likely owners found.
